## Check the log

Open the AppDaemon add-on in Home Assistant and select **Log**, or run the command the deploy script prints:

```sh
ssh root@homeassistant.local ha addons logs a0d7b954_appdaemon
```

Each app logs one line when it loads, with its light, levels, start triggers and test event. For example:

```
INFO bedroom_sunrise: Controls light.bedroom_lamp from sun -6 to 0°, off at 4°. Starts daily at 05:45:00; test with event bedroom_sunrise_start.
```

After that, the app logs each start check, each brightness change and why nothing happened when a start check does nothing. A morning looks like:

```
INFO bedroom_sunrise: Start check (daily at 05:45:00).
INFO bedroom_sunrise: Armed at -9.8°. Ramp runs to 0.
INFO bedroom_sunrise: light.bedroom_lamp to 5%, sun at -9.8°, 0% of the way.
INFO bedroom_sunrise: light.bedroom_lamp to 31%, sun at -3.0°, 70% of the way.
INFO bedroom_sunrise: Ramp done; sun at 1.1°.
INFO bedroom_sunrise: light.bedroom_lamp off over 300 s; sun at 4.0°.
INFO bedroom_sunrise: Disarmed until the next start.
```

Sun updates that change nothing are logged at DEBUG.

A settings mistake shows up here as a validation error naming the bad setting.

## Fire a test event

Each app listens for the event `<app name>_start`. In Home Assistant, go to **Developer Tools > Events**, enter the event type, for example `bedroom_sunrise_start`, and select **Fire event**.

This runs the same check as the app's start trigger. During the fade window the light changes. Outside it the log says why, for example `Not armed: sun at 12.0°, already past -6.`, which still confirms the app is running.
